fcc231580276.name: SR&ED Tax Incentive Program (federal) + Ontario Innovation Tax Credit / Ontario R&D Tax Credit
fcc231580276.funder: Canada Revenue Agency (Department of Finance Canada) and Ontario Ministry of Finance
fcc231580276.deadline: rolling - claim filed with the T2; SR&ED reporting deadline 18 months after fiscal year-end (unchanged)
fcc231580276.amount: Federal: 35% refundable ITC for CCPCs on qualified SR&ED expenditures up to the expenditure limit, now CAD 6M (ENACTED: Bill C-15, Budget 2025 Implementation Act No. 1, royal assent 26 Mar 2026), with the taxable-capital phase-out range raised to CAD 15M-75M; capital expenditures restored to eligibility; enhanced credit extended to eligible Canadian public corporations; applies to taxation years beginning on or after 16 Dec 2024. 15% non-refundable above the limit / for non-CCPCs. Ontario: OITC 8% refundable on up to CAD 3M; ORDTC 3.5% non-refundable (unchanged).
fcc231580276.duration: Annual claim, every fiscal year in which Canadian SR&ED is performed
fcc231580276.eligibility_summary: Any corporation carrying on business in Canada that performs experimental development / applied research IN CANADA with technological uncertainty. The 35% refundable rate requires CCPC status (a private corporation resident in Canada not controlled directly or indirectly by non-residents, public corporations, or a combination). A US-incorporated parent with a Canadian subsidiary can claim on the subsidiary's Canadian R&D but only at the 15% non-refundable rate unless Canadian control exists. Founder citizenship is not the test; founder tax residency and the cap table determine CCPC status. AXIOMALITY's incorporation country, control and Canadian payroll are all unknown, so eligibility cannot be called.
fcc231580276.citizenship_requirement: None for founder; CCPC status depends on control not being held by non-residents (founder residency and cap table matter)
required_documents: Form T661 project descriptions (technological uncertainty, hypotheses, systematic investigation, advancement)
Contemporaneous technical evidence: version-controlled experiment logs, prover/SMT run records, design docs
Payroll records, T4s, contractor invoices, allocation of time to SR&ED
Financial statements and T2 corporate return
fcc231580276.fit_rationale: AXIOMALITY's core work — formal verification of ontology modules, SMT compilation of task checks, physics residuals with conformal calibration, adapters for LeRobot/RLDS/MCAP — is textbook experimental development with genuine technological uncertainty, mapping to O1 (verified ontology) and O2 (audit pipeline). SR&ED is the most reliable recurring non-dilutive source for a Canadian CCPC and stacks with IRAP (IRAP contributions reduce the SR&ED base).
risks_and_flags: Requires Canadian corporation and R&D physically performed in Canada; a US parent with a Canadian sub can still claim on the sub's Canadian R&D
CCPC (35% refundable) status lost if non-residents or a US parent control the company — founder's residency matters
Cash arrives 4–12 months after fiscal year-end; not a substitute for runway
Budget 2025 parameters cited from memory; verify the enacted expenditure-limit figures with CRA before modelling
eligibility_flags: Requires a Canadian corporation (or Canadian subsidiary) with SR&ED physically performed in Canada — incorporation country UNKNOWN

044d578ab514.name: Alexander von Humboldt Research Fellowship (postdoctoral researchers track)
044d578ab514.deadline: rolling (no fixed deadline; selection committee ~3x/year) - unchanged; submit by early Nov 2026 for the ~March 2027 committee
044d578ab514.amount: Monthly fellowship for postdoctoral researchers reported at EUR 3,000 (EUR 3,600 for experienced researchers) by multiple 2026 secondary sources, plus family supplements (~EUR 340/month partner, ~EUR 270/month per child), mobility/travel allowance, language course and a research-cost allowance to the German host. The older EUR 2,670 figure appears to be superseded - confirm the current rate on the Foundation page before quoting.
044d578ab514.duration: 6-24 months in Germany for the postdoctoral track. Correction: the option to split the stay into up to three visits belongs to the experienced-researcher track (6-18 months); the postdoctoral track is a single continuous stay unless the Foundation confirms otherwise.
044d578ab514.eligibility_summary: All nationalities except German (Germans long resident abroad may qualify). Postdoctoral track: doctorate completed less than 4 years before the application is received (Ru: PhD requirements March 2025, so eligible to about March 2029; the formal conferral date on the certificate governs). Above-average publication record in internationally reviewed venues (FOIS, JOWO, ISO work, journal submissions under review may not count until accepted). Applicant must be a researcher from abroad: applicants who have spent more than about 6 months in Germany in the 18 months before applying are excluded (not an issue for Ru). A German host researcher must agree in advance, co-write the research plan, and supply a host statement plus confirmation of research facilities. Fellowship must be taken up physically in Germany, normally within 12 months of the award, and cannot be held concurrently with a Canadian tri-agency award held at U of T.
eligibility_flags: No citizenship barrier - the only unknown that matters is that Ru is not a German national (assumed).

Requires a committed German host before submission; none identified (candidates: Univ. Bremen / DFKI CRC EASE and KnowRob group, Univ. Osnabrueck, TU Dresden, Fraunhofer IPA, LMU/TUM robotics, Hasso Plattner Institute).

Publication-record test: the Foundation weighs peer-reviewed output since the doctorate; the two Synthese papers are still 'submitted' - get at least one accepted or add 2026 conference papers before applying.

Sequencing conflict: a Humboldt stay must be in Germany and cannot overlap a CPRA/U of T postdoc starting spring 2027; realistic slot is either before April 2027 (too soon) or after the Toronto award (2029), which pushes against the 4-year PhD window - decide the sequence before investing 25+ days.
Doctoral certificate is mandatory; the profile lists only 'requirements completed March 2025' - obtain the U of T diploma/transcript showing conferral.

Timing is favourable: committee meetings in March, July and November mean an application filed in Q4 2026 would be decided by March 2027.

2641e31bb744.name: ELLIS postdoctoral positions and mobility (ELLIS Institute Finland postdoc call; unit-level postdocs; ELIAS/ELLIOT-funded mobility exchanges)
2641e31bb744.funder: ELLIS units and institutes (e.g., ELLIS Institute Finland, ELLIS Institute Tübingen, Pioneer Centre for AI Copenhagen); EU projects ELIAS and ELLIOT for mobility
2641e31bb744.deadline: No single deadline. ELLIS Institute Finland: annual postdoc recruitment closed 9 Feb 2026 per the scout; a 2027 round is expected ~Jan-Feb 2027 (unconfirmed). Copenhagen (Pioneer Centre) postdoc listed on ellis.eu closes 30 Sept 2026 per the scout (unconfirmed). Other ELLIS-unit postdocs are posted continuously on ellis.eu/research/jobs. ELIAS/ELLIOT mobility grants are short exchanges (typically 1-6 months) for people already employed at an ELLIS unit.
2641e31bb744.amount: Employment salaries set by the hiring institute (Finnish/German/Danish postdoc pay scales, roughly EUR 45-65k/yr gross); mobility programme covers travel/subsistence for an exchange, not a stipend

The ELLIS postdoc programme's two-unit mobility model requires an ELLIS fellow as primary host and a second ELLIS unit in another country; ELIAS/ELLIOT mobility funding is available to researchers already at partner units. Dr. Ru is eligible to apply for any posting; nothing in the HMS position or Toronto plan blocks an application, but accepting one displaces the Toronto plan.

b6b31033d04d.tier_rationale: Fit is moderate (58) and eligibility is doubtful on three independent unknowns, not one: (1) AXIOMALITY's country of incorporation and cap table (must be a US-located small business >50% owned by US citizens/permanent residents, or by qualifying US small businesses / for SBIR by multiple US VC-operating companies); (2) the PI must be primarily employed (>50%) by the company at award for SBIR, which conflicts with a full-time HMS postdoc and possibly with a J-1/H-1B visa tied to Harvard; (3) the SBIR/STTR statutory authorization lapsed 1 Oct 2025 and neither the reauthorization status nor the existence of a solicitation numbered NSF 26-510 with a 4 Nov 2026 window could be confirmed live. If all three resolve favourably (US entity, compliant cap table, STTR route with Harvard as the 30% research partner so the PI can stay at Harvard), this moves to A for the March 2027 window; the November 2026 window is unrealistic because a Project Pitch invitation (typically 3 weeks turnaround) plus SAM/SBA/Research.gov registrations (4-8 weeks) must precede the proposal.

b6b31033d04d.amount: Phase I up to USD 305,000 (per the last known Phase I solicitation NSF 25-538, incl. optional TABA); Phase II up to ~USD 2,000,000 base; Fast-Track pilot combines Phase I+II. Confirm caps in the live solicitation.
b6b31033d04d.duration: Phase I 6–18 months; Phase II up to 24 months
b6b31033d04d.eligibility_summary: Company must be a for-profit small business located in the US with <500 employees, >50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (or by other qualifying US small businesses; NSF SBIR additionally accepts majority ownership by multiple US VC operating companies / hedge funds / private equity firms, STTR does not). SBIR: PI must be primarily employed by the company (>50% time, at least ~20 h/week) at award and during the award. STTR: PI may be primarily employed by the company OR the partner research institution; at least 40% of the work by the company and at least 30% by a single US non-profit research institution (a US university, FFRDC or non-profit research organization); a Canadian university such as U of T cannot be the STTR partner; Harvard Medical School could, subject to Harvard's founder conflict-of-interest and postdoc-PI policies. A Project Pitch invitation from an NSF program director is mandatory before a full proposal; the pitch is limited to a few hundred words per section and a company may submit a limited number of pitches per window. The proposal PI and company must complete SAM.gov (UEI), SBA Company Registry (SBC ID) and Research.gov registrations before submission. No citizenship requirement on the PI personally, but the ownership test binds the founder's cap table.
